'''Igor R. Klebanov''' (born 1962) is an American [[theoretical physicist]]. Since 1989, he has been a faculty member at [[Princeton University]], where he is currently a Eugene Higgins Professor of Physics and the director of the Princeton Center for Theoretical Science.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Princeton University|url=http://pcts.princeton.edu/people/faculty/1/34|website=pcts.princeton.edu|access-date=2020-05-10|archive-date=December 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206004041/http://pcts.princeton.edu/people/faculty/1/34}}</ref> In 2016, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|department=News from the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|date=May 3, 2016|access-date=2016-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|archive-date=May 6, 2016}}.</ref> Since 2022, he is the director of the Simons Collaboration on Confinement and QCD Strings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2022/06/09/foundation-announces-the-simons-collaboration-on-confinement-and-qcd-strings/|title=Foundation Announces the Simons Collaboration on Confinement and QCD Strings|date=9 June 2022|website=Simons Foundation|access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref>

Klebanov received his undergraduate education at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], class of 1982, and his Ph.D. degree at [[Princeton University]] in 1986 as a student of [[Curtis Callan]].
In his thesis he made advances in the [[Skyrme model]] of [[hadron]]s, which included the first paper on a Skyrmion crystal.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Klebanov | first=Igor | title=Nuclear matter in the skyrme model | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=262 | issue=1 | year=1985 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(85)90068-9 | pages=133–143| bibcode=1985NuPhB.262..133K }}</ref>
Klebanov worked as a post-doc in the [[SLAC Theory Group]].
His main contributions to string theory are in [[String theory|matrix model]] approaches,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gross| first1=David J.| last2=Klebanov | first2=Igor R. | title=One-dimensional string theory on a circle | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=344 | issue=3 | year=1990 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(90)90667-3 | pages=475–498 }}</ref> in [[Membrane (M-theory)|brane]] dynamics, and in the gauge theory-gravity duality.
His work in 1996-97 on relations between branes in [[supergravity]] and their [[gauge theory]] description<ref>{{cite journal | last=Klebanov | first=Igor R. | title=World-volume approach to absorption by non-dilatonic branes | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=496 | issue=1–2 | year=1997 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/s0550-3213(97)00235-6 | pages=231–242| arxiv=hep-th/9702076 | bibcode=1997NuPhB.496..231K | s2cid=17484997 }}</ref> anticipated the gauge theory-gravity correspondence.

Klebanov's 1998 paper<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Gubser | first1=S.S. | last2=Klebanov | first2=I.R. | last3=Polyakov | first3=A.M. | title=Gauge theory correlators from non-critical string theory | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=428 | issue=1–2 | year=1998 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/s0370-2693(98)00377-3 | pages=105–114| arxiv=hep-th/9802109 | bibcode=1998PhLB..428..105G | s2cid=15693064 }}</ref>, Gauge Theory Correlators from Non-Critical String Theory, with his graduate student [[Steven Gubser]], and another Princeton [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Alexander M. Polyakov]], made a precise statement of the [[AdS/CFT]] duality. It is among the top cited papers in theoretical high-energy physics. A series of papers by Klebanov and collaborators on [[D-branes]] on the [[conifold]] has led to discovery<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Klebanov | first1=Igor R | last2=Strassler | first2=Matthew J | title=Supergravity and a confining gauge theory: duality cascades and χSB-resolution of naked singularities | journal=Journal of High Energy Physics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=2000 | issue=8 | date=2000-08-31 | issn=1029-8479 | doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2000/08/052 | page=052| arxiv=hep-th/0007191 | bibcode=2000JHEP...08..052K | s2cid=2484915 }}</ref>  of [[cascading gauge theory]]. Its dual warped throat provides a geometric description of [[color confinement]] and [[chiral symmetry breaking]]; it has been used in model building for cosmology and particle physics. The relation between 3-dimensional critical O(N) model and bosonic higher-spin gauge theory in 4-dimensional AdS space<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Klebanov | first1=I.R | last2=Polyakov | first2=A.M | title=AdS dual of the critical O(N) vector model | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=550 | issue=3–4 | year=2002 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/s0370-2693(02)02980-5 | pages=213–219| arxiv=hep-th/0210114 | bibcode=2002PhLB..550..213K | s2cid=14628213 }}</ref> has been called the Klebanov-Polyakov correspondence.

Klebanov's more recent work includes the Entanglement Entropy in confining gauge theories,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Klebanov | first1=Igor R. | last2=Kutasov | first2=David | last3=Murugan | first3=Arvind | title=Entanglement as a probe of confinement | journal=Nuclear Physics B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=796 | issue=1–2 | year=2008 | issn=0550-3213 | doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2007.12.017 | pages=274–293| arxiv=0709.2140 | bibcode=2008NuPhB.796..274K | s2cid=15648248 }}</ref> the F-theorem for Renormalization Group flows,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Jafferis | first1=Daniel L. | last2=Klebanov | first2=Igor R. | last3=Pufu | first3=Silviu S. | last4=Safdi | first4=Benjamin R. | title=Towards the F-theorem: N = 2 field theories on the three-sphere | journal=Journal of High Energy Physics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=2011 | issue=6 | year=2011 | issn=1029-8479 | doi=10.1007/jhep06(2011)102 | page=| arxiv=1103.1181 | s2cid=117073551 }}</ref> large N tensor models,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Klebanov | first1=Igor R. | last2=Tarnopolsky | first2=Grigory | title=Uncolored random tensors, melon diagrams, and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models | journal=Physical Review D | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=95 | issue=4 | date=2017-02-13 | issn=2470-0010 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.95.046004 | article-number=046004| arxiv=1611.08915 | bibcode=2017PhRvD..95d6004K | s2cid=119391475 }}</ref>  field theory descriptions of critical phenomena, and quantum many-body scars as group invariant states.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Pakrouski | first1=K. | last2=Pallegar | first2=P. N. | last3=Popov | first3=F. K. | last4=Klebanov | first4=I. R. | title=Many-Body Scars as a Group Invariant Sector of Hilbert Space | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=125 | issue=23 | date=2020-12-01 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.125.230602 | article-number=230602| pmid=33337167 | arxiv=2007.00845 | bibcode=2020PhRvL.125w0602P | s2cid=220302660 }}</ref>
